targets.text: Harness hardening and measurement shipped: the pi and qwen bridges (and every checkout bridge) refuse oversized bodies with a 413 instead of desynchronizing the keep-alive connection, a hung pi sync reports the timeout outcome instead of a 500, pi's read-only sandbox mode is enforced at the tool level or refused, CI proves the harness swap by running the §13 conformance kit live against fake-backed pi and qwen bridges with one shared input, deploy.sh recreates api and worker whenever the actor-token set changes, one reviewed command brings a new harness actor online after the root bootstrap, and the harness-compare workflow grades pi, qwen and colleague on the same served model across a declared task set.

every clause of the announcement maps to at least one confirmed requirement (c2-c5, c7-c10, c21) and to a success signal in c27; a clause with no requirement behind it is struck from the announcement, not left as aspiration

oversized-body refusal (#302 item 1): _read_raw_body is byte-identical (md5 72fcf5a7) in pi, qwen, claude-code, codex, colleague, human-inbox and notify server.py and truncates at MAX_BODY_BYTES=8 MiB; notify and human-inbox already ship _refuse_oversized_body (drain in 64 KiB chunks, 413, Connection: close via _write_json(close=True)) — port that helper verbatim to the five checkout bridges and call it before _read_json_body in the invocation handler; jira's server.py already answers 413 at 1 MiB and is untouched

each of the five checkout bridges has a unit test that opens one keep-alive connection, sends a request declaring Content-Length above MAX_BODY_BYTES, receives 413 with Connection: close, and the helper text is byte-identical across the five (diff, not a per-adapter reformat); every server.py stays under 1000 lines

pi sync-timeout escape (#302 item 2): pi_cli.run_sync sends SIGTERM to the process group then calls communicate(timeout=5) with no second TimeoutExpired handler, so an ignoring child surfaces as a generic 500 instead of mapping.CLASS_TIMEOUT; claude_cli.py:252-262, codex_cli.py:365-376 and qwen acp/dispatch.py:229-240 all catch the second timeout and report timed_out=True — pi gains the same guard, and the test uses fake_pi with FAKE_PI_HANG=1 plus a SIGTERM-ignoring variant (fake_claude.py already has FAKE_CLAUDE_IGNORE_SIGTERM for this)

a fake pi that ignores SIGTERM (FAKE_PI_IGNORE_SIGTERM) under a 0.15 s sync timeout returns SyncRunResult.timed_out=True and the handler answers the timeout outcome class, and the child is left running (asserted via its pid file), never SIGKILLed

pi tool-level read-only (#302 item 3): pi 0.85.0 on thor (probed as culture-pi) exposes --tools/-t allowlist and --exclude-tools/-xt denylist over the built-ins read, bash, edit, write; pi_cli.spawn currently does 'del sandbox, mode' while capabilities.py advertises sandbox_modes=('read-only','workspace-write') and server.py validates the value — either build_argv adds --tools read for read-only (soft enforcement, no kernel-boundary claim) or read-only leaves SANDBOX_MODES and the advertised list

build_argv(cfg, instruction, sandbox='read-only') contains '--tools read'; workspace-write contains no --tools flag; the capabilities document's confinement prose says read-only is tool-level and names the flag; a handover dispatch still requires workspace-write (server.py:574 unchanged)

live fake-backed conformance (#297, deviation d2): adapter-pi.yml and adapter-qwen.yml conformance jobs (lines 77-109) run 'go test ./tests/conformance' with no -endpoint; each adapter gains scripts/run_conformance_kit.sh modelled on adapters/claude-code/scripts/run_conformance_kit.sh (start_background on port 0, port file, the kit with -input/-async-input/-bad-input, -expect-callback-retry, -require-cancellation), and both workflows switch to it with the SAME -input JSON so the swap is proven over HTTP

adapters/pi/scripts/run_conformance_kit.sh and adapters/qwen/scripts/run_conformance_kit.sh exist, are executable, pass locally with only go, uv and the fake on the box, and both workflows' conformance job invokes them; the -input, -async-input and -bad-input strings are identical between the two scripts modulo the scratch repo path

deploy.sh recreates api/worker on token change (#300): lanes/two-host.sh thor lane runs 'stop scheduler worker api', 'up -d --scale scheduler=0', 'up -d worker'; the orin lane runs 'up -d' (deploy.sh:927) — none passes --force-recreate, and prod-worker-1 on thor was recreated by hand at 2026-09-04T18:30 (docker inspect) — the lanes recreate api and worker, and tests/test_deploy_two_host.py's shim assertions (_docker(THOR, 'up -d --scale scheduler=0') etc.) move with the new argv

tests/test_deploy_two_host.py asserts that after a run the thor lane's compose argv includes --force-recreate for api and worker and the orin lane's does too, and the live test on thor shows prod-worker-1's Created timestamp move on a deploy with no code change

deploy/prod/README.md's token-rotation runbook (lines 1033-1040) tells the operator to 'docker compose restart worker' after a prod.env change; restart re-uses the existing container and does not re-read --env-file, so the runbook itself reproduces #300 — it changes to the recreate form in the same PR
deploy/prod/README.md contains no 'docker compose ... restart worker' instruction for a token change; the rotation runbook shows the recreate form

first-class cutover command (#298): the manual sequence is bootstrap-accounts.sh (root, stays a hand-turn) → install-secrets.sh (999 lines, one under the 1000-line hard limit in tests/lint/filelength_test.go, so it cannot absorb new logic) → deploy.sh deploy_account_engine_bridge via lanes/account-bridges.sh (455 lines) and lanes/unix-user.sh (643, asserts ~/.pi/agent/models.json) → register-actor.sh with --os-user and harness/model/model_endpoint metadata (README 'Qwen-versus-Pi' section); the command sequences secrets → deploy → register with a dry-run and names every refused step (the #289 posture)

GET /v1alpha1/actors lists company/colleague-spark with harness=colleague and model=unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 metadata; the colleague bridge on spark answers /v1/capabilities; examples/harness-compare compiles with five slots and tests/e2e/harnesscompare_test.go still passes with the unset colleague slot never running

no kernel sandbox returns for pi: frame harness-interop-pi-qwen claim c15 (confirmed) makes the engine account the confinement and capabilities.py's prose says 'pi has no sandbox'; #302 item 3 is tool-level only and never claims a kernel boundary; the Qodo writable_git finding (pi_cli.py:145) was pushed back on the same ground and stays out
no PR in this cycle adds bwrap, docker, or a micro-VM to the pi lane; capabilities.py keeps the 'pi has no sandbox' prose and adds only the tool-level wording

the byte-identical shared modules (preflight.py, deployment.py, dialin.py, reap.py, reclaim.py — tests/lint/preflightsurface_test.go, dialintransport_test.go, workspacereaper_test.go) are not touched; server.py is not a guarded module, but the oversized-body helper is copied verbatim into each bridge rather than formatted per adapter (CLAUDE.md: isort differs across adapters), and server.py sizes are 925/947/941/925/866 lines against the 1000-line limit, so the helper must stay under ~50 lines
tests/lint preflightsurface, dialintransport and workspacereaper guards pass unchanged; diff of the oversized-body helper across the five bridges is empty; go test ./tests/lint filelength passes

all-backends rule (workspace CLAUDE.md): the oversized-body fix lands in every checkout bridge (pi, qwen, claude-code, codex, colleague), not just the two #302 names, because the code is one shared shape and a fix in one backend is a bug

grep for _refuse_oversized_body returns a hit in every adapters/*/src/*/server.py that has an invocation handler (pi, qwen, claude-code, codex, colleague, human-inbox, notify); jira excluded by its own 413

measurements are declarative and re-runnable (refines c19; user direction 2026-09-05): a manifest under examples/harness-compare/measurements/ (YAML authoring, JSON canonical like every other definition here) declares each measurement as a rule — id, category, instruction, an objective check (kind: grep-cites-file-line | seeded-defect-named | tests-named, with its expected value), grade anchors, and runs_per_actor — and a runner reads the manifest, fans every rule across the declared actor set through the harness-compare workflow, applies the check to each run's summary, and posts the anchored grade with the check result in the notes; adding or changing a rule and re-running appends new runs and grades (ledger is append-only), never edits old ones, and a run is tagged with the manifest digest so stats can be read per manifest version. The initial manifest is a BASIC set: one rule per category (locate, review, explain), runs_per_actor 2

the manifest validates against a committed schema; a rule edit changes the manifest digest; the runner refuses a manifest whose digest it cannot compute; re-running the same manifest appends new runs (count rises) and stats per digest are distinguishable; the basic set is exactly one rule per category

the operator running the thor/orin/spark fleet (Ori) and the mesh agents that dispatch to it: every checkout bridge's callers (the worker), the CI reader of the adapter workflows, and the next person bringing a harness online with one command
the delivery summary names which audience each shipped piece served, and the cutover script's --dry-run output was read by the operator before its first real run

today: five checkout bridges desync their keep-alive socket on a body over 8 MiB; a pi child that ignores SIGTERM surfaces as a 500; pi advertises read-only and ignores it; adapter-pi.yml and adapter-qwen.yml prove only the in-process reference actor (deviation d2 needs-follow-up); a deploy after a token change leaves api/worker stale until a hand-typed --force-recreate (#300, counted hand-turn); bringing up four actors in #294 took four hand-run scripts per host (#298); and the harness comparison is one graded run each for pi-thor and qwen-thor with no colleague in the fleet

each before-state clause is reproduced once before the fix lands (a failing test for the desync and the timeout; the d2 record for CI; the #300 and #298 issue bodies for the deploy and cutover; /actors/{id}/stats for the single data point)

after: an oversized body gets a 413 and a closed connection on every checkout bridge; a hung pi sync returns the timeout outcome; sandbox=read-only launches pi with --tools read; CI runs the §13 kit live against fake-backed pi and qwen bridges with one shared input; deploy.sh recreates api and worker in both lanes and the README runbook agrees; deploy/prod/cutover.sh takes a host+engine from secrets to registration with --dry-run and named refusals; a colleague actor is registered on spark and the harness-compare workflow has a fifth slot; and a declared measurement manifest drives graded runs whose per-actor stats are readable per manifest version
each after-state clause is one of the success signals in c27 and is checked in validate-delivery, not asserted in the summary

the #294 cycle proved pi and qwen work by hand; this cycle makes the proof repeatable (CI, deploy, cutover) and the comparison a re-runnable instrument instead of an anecdote — the counted hand-turns (#118) drop by two, and 'which actor is better at what' (#28) gets its first manifest-driven data set
the delivery summary counts the hand-turns removed (#300's recreate, #298's script sequence) against the ones that remain (root bootstrap), and the first manifest run's stats are linked from it

adapter-pi.yml and adapter-qwen.yml conformance jobs are green running go test with -endpoint against a started fake-backed bridge, same -input JSON in both; a unit test per checkout bridge sends a body over MAX_BODY_BYTES on a keep-alive connection and the next request on that connection parses cleanly; test_pi_cli proves a SIGTERM-ignoring fake yields timed_out=True; tests/test_deploy_two_host.py asserts the recreate argv in both lanes; a shim test drives cutover.sh --dry-run end to end and a refused step is named in its output; GET /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/stats for the five actors shows grades in the basic manifest's categories after one manifest run; deviation d2 closes
every signal is a named test, workflow job or API read that validate-delivery can run or fetch; none is a sentence in a summary

bounded drain (challenge / security+concurrency lens): notify's _refuse_oversized_body drains the FULL declared Content-Length before answering 413, and notify's do_POST calls it before any auth check, so an unauthenticated client declaring a huge length can hold the single-threaded server reading for as long as it keeps sending (only the 30 s per-read socket timeout bounds it); the ported helper drains at most MAX_BODY_BYTES (or a small multiple) and then closes, and the same bound goes back into notify and human-inbox so all seven stay identical

a unit test declares Content-Length = 10 * MAX_BODY_BYTES on a keep-alive connection and sends only MAX_BODY_BYTES bytes; the handler answers 413 with Connection: close within the socket timeout without waiting for the rest

grade authority for the manifest runner (challenge / observability+containment lens): internal/api/grades.go makes a human principal's grade land confirmed and an agent's land proposed (nodes-op grade --as defaults to the first kind=human actor); a runner that posts with the operator's identity would mint confirmed human grades by machine, so the runner posts --as its own registered agent actor (e.g. company/measure-runner), grades land proposed with the check result in the notes, and the operator confirms them through the review surface; the runner never uses the human default

GET /v1alpha1/actors lists company/measure-runner with kind=agent; every grade a manifest run posts is authority=proposed and origin=agent in the ledger; the runner never calls nodes-op grade with a human actor as the grader

the manifest records what was actually measured (challenge / lifecycle lens): thor/orin bridges are uv-tool-install copies that only change on deploy.sh, and pi under --tools read behaves differently from the pi that earned the existing 4/5; each run therefore carries the rule's sandbox and each actor's bridge revision (the deployment block on /v1/capabilities), read before dispatch, and the runner refuses an actor whose revision is behind the merged main revision the manifest run expects
each manifest run's input carries sandbox and per-actor bridge revisions; the runner exits non-zero naming the stale actor when a /v1/capabilities revision differs from the expected one

fifth slot in the proof (challenge / overlooked-actors lens): tests/e2e/harnesscompare_test.go pins harnessCompareSlots = {claude, codex, pi, qwen} and a registry map of slot -> actor key; the colleague slot joins both, the compile test asserts five guarded agent nodes, and the two-actor run asserts the unset colleague slot never ran
go test ./tests/e2e -run TestHarnessCompare passes with five slots declared and the colleague slot unset

cutover.sh preconditions and idempotency (challenge / rollback lens): the compose files' api and worker environment blocks must already declare the actor token key for the engine and host (the NODES_ACTOR_..._TOKEN name register-actor.sh is given; a committed change no runtime script can make) and the engine account must exist on the host; cutover.sh checks both first and refuses by name; every step it runs is idempotent (install_bridge_account_env keeps an existing token unless the engine's FORCE flag is set, deploy_account_engine_bridge re-installs the same revision, register-actor.sh inserts a revision only when state differs) so a re-run after a partial failure converges, and --dry-run reports 'would skip' for steps already done

a shim test runs cutover.sh twice against the same fake host: the second run's log shows every step skipped and the exit is 0; a run against a compose file missing the token key exits non-zero naming the key
